name: Tatneft
verdict: Tied to the government of the Republic of Tatarstan: its holding Svyazinvestneftekhim is Tatneft's largest shareholder and Tatarstan holds a golden share over Tatneft.
note: Rating note: propose a tier above 'none' (state with a record controls the sponsor: golden share + 27.2% of capital via the wholly republic-owned Svyazinvestneftekhim; chain tatneft → government-of-tatarstan → russian-federation, whose record claim documents the war in Ukraine). Mirrors the Gazprom/Aeroflot pattern for Russian state-controlled sponsors. Placement evidence: TATNEFT wordmark on the front of the 2026/27 home jersey in the KHL's official season renders (sports.ru 'КХЛ.Маркетинг', 13 Sep 2026); the club site's live sponsor data lists Tatneft as general sponsor. Leads, not recorded as claims: (1) Stavka TV (updated 2 May 2026) says the club is operated by LLC SKP 'Tatneft – Ak Bars' whose sole owner is Tatneft — club ownership, not a kit sponsor; (2) РБ Бизнес (via bookmaker-rating.com) reported Tatneft cut funding to Ak Bars by ~₽600m in 2025 — no per-year value readable, so no deal record. TAdviser gives Tatarstan's stake as 34% where Tatneft's own page gives 27.23%/29.07%; the claim uses the company's figures.

why.text: Tatneft's largest shareholder is Svyazinvestneftekhim — 27.2% of capital, 29.1% of votes — a holding whose sole shareholder is the Republic of Tatarstan, and Tatarstan holds a 'golden share' over Tatneft under its charter. The Russian Federation, at the top of that chain, launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and has been at war with Ukraine since. A famous shirt makes the state behind the sponsor look good to millions of fans while that goes on. That’s called sportswashing.
why.messageLine: Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022 and has been at war with Ukraine since.
